sentences.text:
Shri Vishnu Kumar Upadhyay - Advocate for the appellant
 Shri Yash Soni - Public Prosecutor for the respondent/S
Heard on I.A.No.17140 of 2025, which is the sixth application under Section 430(1) of the Bnss,
2023/389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

His first and fifth applications were dismissed for want of prosecution vide orders dated 24.10.2018
and 01.10.2024 respectively, second, third and fourth applications were dismissed as withdrawn
vide orders dated 15.02.2019, 30.08.2019 and 14.08.2020 respectively.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 29.06.2017 passed by XI Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District Jabalpur (M.P.) in S.T. No.474/2015, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction Imprisonment Fine

entities.text: XI Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District Jabalpur (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In lieu of default U/s.
Additi. R.I. for 302 of IPC Life Imprisonment Rs.2,000/-
 
 
 498A of IPC R.I. for 02 years Rs.1,000/-
Learned counsel for appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that as per the prosecution case, the allegation against the present appellant is of setting the deceased ablaze by pouring kerosene over her due to which the deceased 2 CRA-2628-2017 succumbed to the burn injuries sustained.

The appellant is in jail and has already undergone more than 12 years of incarceration therefore, in the light of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh [SLP (Cri.)
No.4633/2021], the application may be considered on the ground of period of incarceration.

sentences.text:
Hence,
it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh (supra) as well as the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellant, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear 3 CRA-2628-2017 before the Registry of this Court on 20.01.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (RATNESH CHANDRA SIN  JUDGE JUDGE  SSL Chhotu Alias Sandeep vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169346497/
